transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Lately, I've been having a really hard time listening when people are talking directly to me. My friends and family keep complaining that I'm zoning out or not paying attention, even when we're in the middle of a conversation. It's getting pretty frustrating, so I wanted to see if I could get some help with it.
Do you also find yourself being overly restless, fidgety, interrupting others, or acting without thinking, or is it mainly trouble paying attention?

Honestly, it's a mix of both. I constantly feel restless inside, find it really hard to do quiet activities, and struggle with waiting my turn. On top of that, I have a terrible time organizing my tasks and constantly forget daily chores and appointments.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation), Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation), Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Major Depressive Disorder, Adjustment Disorder], but the patient now endorses both significant inattentive symptoms (zoning out, poor organization, forgetfulness) and hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (restlessness, difficulty with quiet activities, waiting turn), which makes predominantly inattentive ADHD less likely and supports ADHD Combined Presentation. Anxiety, depression, and adjustment disorder are less supported because the symptoms described are core attentional/impulsivity problems rather than primarily worry, low mood, or a situational stress reaction.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports prominent inattentive symptoms (difficulty sustaining attention in conversation, disorganization, forgetfulness) along with hyperactive/impulsive symptoms (inner restlessness, difficulty with quiet activities, trouble waiting turn). This pattern best fits ADHD, Combined Presentation rather than predominantly inattentive or hyperactive/impulsive types.
